messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a spike of 'unexpected EOF' and half-streamed chat responses from the Android SDK running on older devices (API 21-24) after ~30s of streaming.

maya: ugh. on which layer? okhttp or retrofit?

alex: looks like OkHttp connection reuse + our call/read timeouts + coroutine cancellation interplay. Logs show socket closed by peer mid-stream. Happens reliably when user backgrounded the app and OS freezes network briefly.

jordan: does it happen with HTTP/2 only?

alex: mostly when http2 is enabled. hypothesis: server sends Connection: close for long-poll/stream edges, okhttp tries to reuse, coroutine cancellation races with response body reading.

sam: can you paste the minimal stack/log lines?

alex: sure — here's a snippet from logcat and the okhttp debug line:

```
E/OkHttp: unexpected end of stream
E/ChatClient: java.io.EOFException: 
 at okio.BufferedSource.read(BufferedSource.java:xxx)
 at okhttp3.internal.http1.Http1Codec.readResponseBody(Http1Codec.java:xxx)
 at okhttp3.internal.http.CallServerInterceptor.intercept(CallServerInterceptor.java:xxx)
 Caused by: java.net.SocketException: socket closed
```

maya: thanks. we saw similar on low mem devices a while back. Workarounds?

jordan: couple things to try: 1) set callTimeout > readTimeout so cancellations propagate better; 2) disable connection pooling for streaming calls or set connectionPool().evictAll() after heavy streams; 3) force okhttp to use HTTP/1.1 for streaming endpoints as temp measure.

sam: can we toggle per-request? retrofit + okhttp supports newBuilder on client but rotation per-call is annoying. One trick is an interceptor that adds header `Connection: close` for streaming paths.

alex: tried adding header, reduced EOFs by ~80% in our internal stress tests. downside: loses keep-alive for the route.

maya: any SDK-level changes we should make for parity with other clients? i.e., JS/python handle stream reconnects gracefully.

jordan: we could expose streaming config on the SDK: allow `streamingPolicy` with options {useHttp1, connectionCloseHeader, callTimeoutMs}. Default stays conservative. Docs + samples needed.

sam: +1. Also add guidance for Android: prefer setting pingInterval() on OkHttp for http2 when in foreground. For backgrounded apps the OS might suspend pings though.

alex: posted a tiny sample fix in the test app — toggles `Connection: close` for devices <= API 24 and uses call timeout tweaks. results looked solid.

maya: can you open a PR with sample and a short note in the migration guide? tag eng-runtime if any server changes required.

alex: will do. PR will include: sample code, textarea about perf tradeoffs, and a small junit/instrumentation test that simulates pause/resume.

ci-bot: build passed for branch/feature/android-stream-evict (job #412). :white_check_mark:

sam: follow-up item — add a small telemetry flag so we can count EOFs by device API and http version. then we can flip strategy when majority on newer devices.

jordan: filed a ticket in backlog: DEVEX-8423 — "Android SDK: streaming EOFs on older OS; add streamingPolicy + telemetry".

maya: great. for now add the workaround snippet to the quickstart Android guide so customers with mobile chat apps see it.

alex: thanks all — I'll include the snippet here for quick copy:

```
// OkHttp builder tweak for streaming endpoints
OkHttpClient base = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .pingInterval(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS) // helps http2 when app foregrounded
  .callTimeout(2, TimeUnit.MINUTES)
  .readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) // streaming
  .build();

// Per-request header when targeting older Android
Request newReq = original.newBuilder()
  .header("Connection", "close")
  .build();
```

maya: perfect. short blurb + link to ticket and PR is enough. I'll add to the guide after PR lands. :thumbsup:

alex: cool, filing PR now. thanks everyone.
